main_text.l: lentius se invenisse ait. Habet autē eorum
mistura hoc pacto. Aloes, scammonij, gum-
mi, colocynthidis, bdellij, singulorū femun-
cia. Capiat ex his æger pro viribus scrupu-
los tres, aut quatuor: Nec comitialibus mo-
dò, sed etiam vertiginosis & articularis, si
quid aliud, auxiliantur: Excipiantur autem
succo brasicæ. Post apophlegmatismis, &
gargarismis cerebrum à crasis & viscidis
excrementis expurgari præcipit. Vomitio-
nes quoq; præseruationis gratia, plurimū
commendat, siue ante cibos, siue abipsis
excitentur: propterea quòd ea discutiant
& euacuent, quæ in stomacho crassa & vi-
scida inhærent. Hæc sunt in genere phar-
maca, quib. hactenus usi sunt medici præcla-
riores ad primarii morbi comitialis profli-
gationem. Veruntamen quoniam à variis
excitari causis solet: Idcirco singulis suum
peculiare remedium asignare licet. Itaque
si à sanguine oboriatur, & tum nullus adsit
spasmus,
primùm sanguis ex interna
stri cubiti vena mittendus est: dein exis,
quæ sunt iuxta talum eiusdem lateris, tan-
dem ex utroq; crure. Occipitio affigendæ
cucurbitulæ: vel ea pars candente ferro in-
urenda, ut inde continuò effluat sanies.

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. The word "præcla-" at the line end is partly worn in the scan but reads as præclariores continued on the next line. The abbreviation "dō" is read from a faint macron. The running head and page number are printed at the top; the N and Quòd at the foot are signature and catchword.
